properties.name: Cabanatuan Branch (Bigaa/Balagtas – Baliuag – Gapan – Cabanatuan)
properties.wartime_notes: Reopened May 14, 1942; major rice-bowl artery serving Bulacan and Nueva Ecija (and near Cabanatuan POW Camp). Upper sections torn up/dismantled in 1944–1945; not rebuilt to Cabanatuan until 1969.

properties.name: Tarlac – San Jose Branch (Tarlac – Victoria – Guimba – Muñoz – San Jose)
properties.operator_wwii: Imperial Japanese Army Riku'un Kanrikyoku; US Army (1945)
properties.wartime_notes: MRR's newest pre-war branch (completed Feb 1939 toward Cagayan Valley). Active during WWII and strategically used in 1945 Central Luzon / Balete Pass operations.

properties.name: Tayug / San Quintin Branch (Paniqui – Cuyapo – Rosales – San Quintin)
properties.wartime_notes: Served eastern Pangasinan and northern Nueva Ecija. Rosales–San Quintin section abandoned/dismantled by 1945; Paniqui–Rosales survived into post-war decades.

properties.name: Arayat Branch (San Fernando, Pampanga – Mexico – Arayat)
properties.wartime_notes: Served central Pampanga sugar and agricultural districts east of San Fernando.

properties.name: Carmen / Floridablanca Branch (San Fernando, Pampanga – Guagua – Lubao – Del Carmen)
properties.operator_wwii: Imperial Japanese Army Riku'un Kanrikyoku; US Army (1945)
properties.wartime_notes: Connected PASUDECO (San Fernando) and PASUMIL (Del Carmen) sugar centrals and western Pampanga approaches toward Bataan.

properties.name: Fort Stotsenburg / Clark Field Military Branch (Dau – Margot – Fort Stotsenburg)
properties.operator_wwii: Imperial Japanese Forces (Clark Air District, 1942–1945); US Army (1945)
properties.wartime_notes: Strategic military branch serving Fort Stotsenburg and Clark Field air complex (~8.8 km west from Dau). Heavily fought over during Dec 1941 attack and Jan 1945 liberation.
properties.source: Reconstructed from BLS SL 33, US Army official history & OSM town coordinates

properties.name: Magalang Branch (Dau – Sapang Biabas – Bical – Magalang)
properties.operator_wwii: Imperial Japanese Army Riku'un Kanrikyoku (damaged/abandoned during WWII)
properties.wartime_notes: 8.8 km agricultural branch running east-northeast from Dau to Magalang (active in 1939 MRR timetable; not restored after WWII).
properties.source: OpenStreetMap (OSM abandoned ROW ways 1244813262–1244813275) & OSM town coordinates

properties.name: Batangas Branch (Calamba – Tanauan – Malvar – Lipa – Batangas)
properties.operator_wwii: Imperial Japanese Army Riku'un Kanrikyoku; US Army (1945)
properties.wartime_notes: Served southern Laguna and Batangas (Lipa airfields & Batangas port). Note: Batangas–Bauan extension had closed in 1936 and Malvar–San Pablo cut-off closed April 1941.

properties.name: Santa Cruz – Pagsanjan Branch (College – Bay – Magdalena – Santa Cruz – Pagsanjan)
properties.wartime_notes: Eastern Laguna branch off College (Los Baños). Santa Cruz–Pagsanjan section closed/dismantled during WWII (1942); College–Santa Cruz partially operated and briefly restored post-war.

properties.name: Canlubang – Buntog Branch (Mamatid – Majada – Canlubang – Buntog)
properties.operator_prewar: Manila Railroad Company / Calamba Sugar Estate
properties.operator_wwii: Imperial Japanese Forces; returned to MRR by 1946
properties.wartime_notes: Served Canlubang (Calamba Sugar Estate) and surrounding agricultural/airfield sites; listed in 1939 Southern Lines timetable and still active in 1946.
properties.source: OpenStreetMap (OSM abandoned ROW) & BLS SL 33 station coordinates

properties.name: Santa Mesa – Mandaluyong – Fort McKinley (Guadalupe) Branch
properties.division: Manila Suburban — Surviving Antipolo Line Segment
properties.wartime_notes: Surviving western portion of the old Antipolo Line connecting Santa Mesa to Mandaluyong and Fort McKinley (Antipolo section closed 1918; Montalban closed 1936; Pasig–Taytay closed 1941). Used in Dec 1941/Jan 1942 USAFFE locomotive denial demolitions near Pasig River.

properties.name: Manila Port & Santibañez (Isla Provisor) Freight Spurs
properties.wartime_notes: Critical Manila industrial/port freight spurs linking Pandacan across Pasig River swing bridge to Isla Provisor / Tabacalera and Tutuban to North Harbor / Port Area.
